svg.title: Event Loop Summary: Node vs. Others
svg.desc: Auto-playing 64s step-by-step explainer of "Event Loop Summary: Node vs. Others" (from img_9.png). Each step is highlighted in turn with what happens, why it matters, missing concepts added in lime, and a Node.js code example. Hover to pause.
svg.text: Event Loop Summary: Node vs. Others
One thread with an event loop vs. one thread per user, and the golden rule: DON'T BLOCK!
Sync is OK at startup only

g.text: Event Loop Summary: Node vs. Others
What: Node serves every user on ONE thread with an event loop and offloads heavy work.
Apache + PHP classically create a NEW THREAD per user.
Why: Node's model is lighter, but it puts responsibility on you: if your code blocks the
Added: How to fix blocking code and how to measure event-loop lag.
user2 ─┼─► SINGLE THREAD user2 ─► NEW THREAD
user3 ─┤ + event loop user3 ─► NEW THREAD
user4 ─┘ ─► thread pool user4 ─► NEW THREAD
cheap per user, but isolated per user, but
DON'T BLOCK the one thread costs RAM per thread
What: All requests share one thread. While a request waits for I/O, the thread handles other
Why: Thousands of mostly-waiting connections fit in very little memory.
const rows = await db.query('SELECT ...'); // thread is free
What: Classic servers give each request its own thread or process. Simple and isolated, but
each one costs memory and mostly sits idle waiting for I/O.
Added: Modern PHP (PHP-FPM, Nginx) reuses a pool of workers, but the model is still one
1 JS thread + event loop + small pool
→ but ONE slow callback delays all 10 000
What: Don't use sync versions of functions in the fs, crypto and zlib modules inside your
Why: A sync call holds the only thread until it finishes; every other user is frozen.
// ✗ blocks EVERY user while the file is read
What: Don't do complex calculations (loops inside loops), be careful with JSON.parse /
stringify of large objects, and avoid regexes with nested quantifiers.
Added: A bad regex is a security bug (ReDoS): one crafted input string can freeze your whole
// ✗ parsing a 200 MB string freezes the server
What: Use async APIs and streams, move CPU work to worker_threads, split long loops into
chunks, or push heavy jobs to a queue processed elsewhere.
// split a big loop so other callbacks get turns
What: Measure event-loop delay: how late callbacks run compared to when they should. Rising
What: Node = one thread for everyone. That is fast and cheap only as long as no callback
Added: Fixes (async, streams, workers, chunking, queues), ReDoS, and measuring loop lag.
[ ] no nested-quantifier regex on user input

svg.text: One slow callback slows down every user
Q: How do you handle CPU-heavy work in Node?
A: worker_threads, job queue, or chunking
